title: Does a local MP get a local bonus?
excerpt: Parties now pick far more local candidates. Across every MP elected since 1832, being born near the seat wins about 1.3 points more of the vote, but has not made local MPs any less likely to lose.
seo_description: Do MPs born near their seat win more votes? 31,737 MP returns since 1832: about 1.3 points more, but no fewer defeats.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Does a local MP get a local bonus?' beside a map of Great Britain with a dot for every constituency coloured by the share of its MPs born locally, and the line 'about 1.3 points more of the vote, but no fewer defeats'.
